observations:
Torah #77 does not meet the threshold for new package proposals. The criterion requires 3 or more concepts with explicit bechina language forming an independent domain not covered by existing packages.

The surviving fragment of Torah #77 yields at most 2 bechina pairs:
  (1) הֶבֶל פֶּה ↔ אוֹת הֵ"א — already in dataset (reference=77, type=bechina)
  (2) קוֹל ↔ אוֹת וָ"ו — present in source text, flagged as addition, NOT yet in dataset

Even if both pairs were fully encoded in the dataset, they would form two separate 2-node components, not a single domain of 3+ nodes. They are structurally parallel (each maps a speech-element to its corresponding letter of the divine Name) and could plausibly be grouped into a single 'Sacred Speech Letters' package — but this requires only that the קוֹל ↔ אוֹת וָ"ו edge be added to the dataset first. The package would then be:
  Component: {הֶבֶל פֶּה, אוֹת הֵ"א, קוֹל, אוֹת וָ"ו} — 4 nodes, but sharing only indirect connections (heh connects to vapor, vav connects to voice; heh and vav are not themselves bechina-connected in the surviving fragment). Until the second bechina pair is confirmed and added, no multi-node domain of 3+ exists.

More fundamentally, Torah #77 is explicitly documented as almost entirely lost ('חָסֵר כָּאן רֻבּוֹ כְּכֻלּוֹ'). The surviving 5-line fragment is a summary introduction, not the body of the teaching. Any new package proposed on this basis would rest on a fragment of a fragment. Proposing new packages from lost teachings risks fabricating structure that may be entirely inconsistent with the Rebbe's original intent.

Conclusion: No new packages should be proposed for Torah #77. When/if more complete manuscript sources for this Torah become available, the analysis should be rerun from scratch using the full text.

Note on thematic domain: The surviving fragment addresses the letters of the divine Name (י-ה-ו-ה) and their correspondence to the organs of sacred speech (breath/heh, voice/vav, and by implication yud and heh-final through dechilu-u-rechilu). This domain — divine Name letters and sacred speech — is not a new independent domain in the Likutey Moharan corpus; it appears in multiple other Torahs. If the lost body of Torah #77 is ever recovered, this domain would likely form a central package, but it cannot be proposed on the basis of surviving evidence alone.
